reflection: Explain one choice to a partner.
title: Animal Diets
description: Sort real animal photographs in two wildlife notebook challenges, using clues and explanations.
brief: Sort six animals by their usual wild diets. What evidence supports each choice?

items.label: African elephant
items.clue: Pulls up grass and reaches for leaves, bark and fruit.
items.why: African elephants are herbivores. Grass, leaves, bark, roots and fruit all come from plants.

items.label: Giraffe
items.clue: Uses a long tongue to reach leaves high in trees.
items.why: Giraffes are herbivores. They browse leaves and other plant parts, often high above the ground.

items.label: Lion
items.clue: Hunts animals such as antelope and zebra.
items.why: Lions are carnivores. Their usual wild diet comes from animals, including antelope and zebra.

items.label: Tiger
items.clue: Hunts deer, wild pigs and other animals.
items.why: Tigers are carnivores. Deer and wild pigs are examples of the animals they hunt for food.

items.label: Raccoon
items.clue: Finds fruit and nuts, along with insects, crayfish and eggs.
items.why: Raccoons are omnivores. Fruit and nuts are plant foods; insects, crayfish and eggs come from animals.

items.label: Brown bear
items.clue: Eats berries and roots, as well as insects, fish and other animals.
items.why: Brown bears are omnivores. They eat plant foods and animal foods; what they find changes with the season and location.

items.label: European rabbit
items.clue: Nibbles grass, leaves, buds and roots.
items.why: European rabbits are herbivores. Grass, leaves, buds and roots are all plant foods.

items.label: Plains zebra
items.clue: Spends much of its feeding time grazing on grass.
items.why: Plains zebras are herbivores. They mostly graze on grass and may also eat leaves and stems.

items.label: Grey wolf
items.clue: Hunts animals such as deer, elk and smaller mammals.
items.why: Grey wolves are carnivores. Their usual diet includes large grazing animals and smaller mammals.

items.label: Nile crocodile
items.clue: Catches fish and other animals near the water.
items.why: Nile crocodiles are carnivores. Fish, birds and mammals are animal foods.

items.label: Red fox
items.clue: Catches mice and insects, and also eats fruit.
items.why: Red foxes are omnivores. Mice and insects are animals, while fruit comes from plants. Hunting does not make their whole diet carnivorous.

items.label: Wild boar
items.clue: Roots around for nuts, roots, insects, worms and eggs.
items.why: Wild boars are omnivores. Roots and nuts are plant foods; insects, worms and eggs are animal foods.

rounds.label: Meet the animals
rounds.brief: Sort six animals by their usual wild diets. What evidence supports each choice?
rounds.reflection: Choose one omnivore. Name a plant food and an animal food it eats.

rounds.label: Look more closely
rounds.brief: Six new animals. Does an animal that hunts always belong with the carnivores?
rounds.reflection: Why does the red fox belong with the omnivores? Use two examples from its diet.

notes:
Learning focus: classify using evidence, explain a choice, then revise. Each challenge includes two herbivores, two carnivores and two omnivores.

Before the sort: invite students to predict. Reveal field notes when they need evidence, then check their sort. Ask partners to explain one choice that changed.

Useful distinctions: insects are animals. Red foxes and brown bears eat both plant and animal foods. Bear species have different diets. These groups describe the selected animals’ usual wild diets; they do not mean that every individual eats exactly the same things all the time.

Sources: each feedback card links to its animal profile from San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance or the University of Michigan’s Animal Diversity Web.
